## What it is

An editable, named-component reconstruction of the Neewer GM-MP2 140 mm macro focusing rail. The rotating top Arca clamp exposes 0, 90, 180, and 270-degree detents. Use `arca_0_deg` for the captured scan pose and `reference_photo` for the illustrative deployed feet, installed camera plate, six pads, camera stud and original focus knob without the custom sleeve. The default keeps the 90-degree clamp and supplied sleeve accessory.

The manufacturer specifies 140 mm carriage travel, four 90-degree rotation locks, double Arca quick release, 1/4-inch and 3/8-inch mounting points, 512 g mass, and 2.5 kg payload. Source: https://neewer.com/products/neewer-gm-mp2-140mm-macro-focusing-rail-slider-with-360-rotation-66606520

## Design notes

- The reconstructed base, controls, guide shafts, carriage, rotary connector, jaws, lock tab, folding feet and visible fasteners remain separately selectable components. Per-component appearance distinguishes black anodized bodies, silver shafts and controls, dark pads and cap, white markings, and the amber custom sleeve accessory.
- The calibrated origin is x=33.15 mm and the scan carriage position is 70.35 mm, preserving the observed pivot at (103.5, 22.10675, 28.0) mm. Scan sections fit carriage end faces x=81.69 and 125.66 mm, while stationary end blocks terminate at x=11.31 and 195.34 mm. The resulting nominal endpoint gaps are approximately 0.03 mm, below the estimated ±0.4 mm scan uncertainty; this is coherent CAD travel, not verification of physical stop clearance. Every attached clamp and optional plate component follows the requested travel and detent.
- The bottom mounting interface follows repeated scan sections. Its upper side-rail shells remain continuous from x=0.75 to 206.0 mm. The lower dovetail tongue and return occupy x=0.75..10.0, 31.75..175.25, and 197.5..206.0 mm, and are absent in the folded-foot bays at x=10.0..31.75 and 175.25..197.5 mm. The interval transitions have an estimated uncertainty of ±0.25 mm. The remaining 46-degree engagement flanks stay sharp; six lower-web slots and two upper-web windows retain the observed openings between the side rails.
- The top clamp follows the scanned 49.1 by 54.25 mm footprint. Its fixed and movable jaws form a 37.9 mm upper opening and 42.8 mm seat opening with fixed and movable flanks at 63.95 and 59.04 degrees from horizontal, respectively, and the two open-ended pockets retain the measured 36.95 mm floor. Their curved ends fit radius 6.36 mm at x=90.50 and 116.31 mm, y=22.01 mm. The shallow capsule recesses have floors z=39.20 and 39.13 mm; they are recesses, not raised pads in the scan. Only outward corners are softened; the mating flank coordinates stay unchanged.
- `references/neewer-outer-focus-sleeve.step` is preserved as exact B-rep geometry and placed on the scan-derived large-knob axis. Its outer cylinder is 22 mm diameter and 5 mm wide; its eightfold opening is the authoritative tight-fit interface.
- Fitting that opening to the scan gave 0.097 mm median radial clearance (about 0.19 mm diametral) and 0.093 mm RMS residual. Tiny negative patches remain, so these scan-derived fit values stay provisional.
- The assembly declares the modeled large-knob/sleeve pair with a 0.05 mm CAD clearance requirement. The current exact shapes have a 0.089 mm minimum gap and no positive-volume intersection. This continuously protects the CAD relationship; it does not certify manufactured clearance.
- Scan-derived values in `measurements.toml` remain provisional. Broad observed ribs, recesses and shoulders are reconstructed; triangle noise, fine pad texture, cosmetic knurling and unknown lead-screw threads are omitted. White scale labels and the NEEWER wordmark use deterministic stroke geometry as a cosmetic approximation. The optional camera stud uses nominal 1/4-20 geometry with 1.27 mm pitch; that standard depiction is not a pitch measurement from the scan.
- The two folding feet reproduce the observed bay envelopes and rounded undersides. `feet_deployed` selects a provisional 65-degree swing about seam-derived pivots; the concealed hinge and physical stop were not measured. A continuous swing accommodation is cut into the same stationary base and end blocks in every displayed state. No hidden hinge pins are invented. The receiver cavities retain blind shaft seats and add a provisional 0.05 mm radial allowance about the existing independently fitted shaft and knob axes. These are coherent CAD mechanisms, not recovered manufactured bearings.
- The supplied scan captures the top Arca clamp in its longitudinal 0-degree detent with the camera plate removed. `camera_plate_installed` adds a nominal 68 mm photo-inferred plate, six separate pads and camera stud. `include_sleeve` controls the supplied custom sleeve, which is not original manufacturer hardware. The hidden bearing bores, rotary socket and nominal camera-plate fit are provisional mechanical allowances, not measured internal geometry.
- The stored `.ply.gz` is a deterministic geometry-only binary PLY conversion of the supplied `neewer-macro-slide-GM-MP2.stl`. It preserves all 126,072 vertices, 252,204 faces, bounds, and area from the repaired watertight STL; the source STL SHA-256 is `1d134187bd303830bd58c082fa5f4268afb295ea5a70fbf575cf312dcc17f5c7`.
- `references/neewer-arca-sections.svg` shows current CAD and reference sections at a solid bottom-plate station, a folded-foot bay, and the top clamp in the scan pose. `references/neewer-current-acceptance.json` binds the results to model and both helper sources, validator, measurements, acceptance-specification, generated-geometry, source STEP, and PLY.GZ hashes plus the exact parameters. Present bottom contact flanks have 0.17 to 0.23 mm scan-distance p95, the top jaw flanks have 0.55 to 0.61 mm p95, and bay-centre sections independently show the lower flank missing. These are feature-local results at the declared 0.75 mm band; unverified details and optional configurations make whole-model coverage inappropriate.
- Run `python references/validate_reconstruction.py` after changing the model. It builds all 12 combinations of four detents and minimum/middle/maximum travel, compares each attached component's full B-rep vertex set and Location in the rotary-base frame, checks the static sleeve fit, reproduces the Arca evidence, and reopens the printable sleeve's STEP source plus temporary STL and 3MF exports. It exits nonzero and preserves the last accepted evidence on failure. Use `--check-report` for a read-only current/stale result and run `python references/test_validator_regressions.py` for the normal and `python -O` deliberate-clearance failures.

## Don't

- Do not replace the exact outer-focus sleeve with a traced mesh or a circular guess.
- Do not describe photo-inferred dimensions or nominal standard hardware as scan measurements or verified manufacturer dimensions.
- Do not assess whole-model deviation in the default operating pose; compare the `arca_0_deg` variant.

## Changelog

- 2026-09-30: Fitted curved clamp pockets, shallow strips, outer bearing housings and controls; added explicit rotary support, shaft passages, visible lock and hardware, articulated feet, optional photo-style plate, calibrated travel, component appearance and reproducible local evidence.

- 2026-09-22: Hardened acceptance against disabled assertions, bound evidence to its validator and measurement specification, added a read-only freshness check, and added model-specific failure regressions.
- 2026-09-22: Fixed the clamp attachment to follow carriage travel, declared the exact sleeve fit, and added revision-specific motion and Arca-section acceptance evidence.
- 2026-09-21: Corrected the bottom Arca lower dovetail around the measured folded-foot bays and exposed named 0, 90, 180, and 270-degree top-clamp variants.
- 2026-09-21: Rebuilt the scan as a parametric named-component assembly with the exact STEP sleeve, scan-section-derived bottom Arca plate and top clamp, 90-degree Arca detents, and saved scan pose.
